scope: Source and live issue/PR investigation of agent-harness sandbox integration and Omnigent reuse. No implementation, configuration change, review-seat launch, credential access or cloud provisioning.
conclusion: Omnigent contains reusable sandbox provider lifecycle, managed host/session infrastructure, Linux/macOS tool confinement and secretless credential/egress proxy implementations. It is not a conformant agent-harness ExecutingBackend or proof that subscription TUI seats satisfy the declared profiles. Prefer adapters around upstream primitives rather than rebuilding vendor provisioning in agent-harness, while retaining harness admission, snapshot and lease evidence.

current_state.finding: The remote placement driver and lease journal merged in agent-harness#1492, but launch-site flag _NONLOCAL_EXECUTION_DRIVER is false. No concrete remote backend or reconnect ships in that change.
Latest remote plan sequences self-hosted SSH first, then reconnect, placed Claude, and Codex/Grok subordinate-uid placement; cloud remains follow-on. Replacing that order would be a plan change.

Active v11 replaces retired EC-HARDEN-5 with EC-HARDEN-6: seat capabilities are declared, authorized and recorded. The old SBXEXEC/SBXFETCH/SBXSEAT separation design is proposal-only and must not be confused with today's admission target.

Codex tool startup has independent nested namespace and staged-tree write permission problems. agent-harness#1489 is an open targeted fix for agent-harness#1470; changing sandbox suppliers does not establish the fix.
Gemini tooled jail remains unqualified because inference and other Google APIs share front-end IPs; existing IP-based filtering cannot distinguish them.

Existing Omnigent board backing is frozen to v0.4, intended for breadth harnesses, and no production from_env/from_config caller was found. Its default session creation does not request managed sandbox placement.
Our TypeScript agent-harness adapter is request/result mapping; it does not provision a sandbox.

upstream_reuse.name: Provider lifecycle
provides: optional file copy, captured execution, streaming execution and foreground execution
limits: Capabilities are provider declarations, not destination-bound proof of confinement.
Managed-only providers do not promise arbitrary exec/put transport.
No owner/lease fencing or snapshot receipt contract in the general launcher API.

upstream_reuse.name: Managed hosts and cleanup
provides: idle keepalive and generation-aware cleanup retries
optional retained storage and Kubernetes warm-pool allocation
limits: Provider lifetimes and cost cleanup settings require explicit configuration.
General managed session startup clones repositories; a review must instead use the exact revalidated staged snapshot.

upstream_reuse.name: Tool confinement and credential proxy
provides: Linux mount/network namespace and seccomp tool sandbox
TLS-inspecting egress with method/path rules and private-destination denial
parent-held credentials, host-bound injection and optional placeholders
limits: These mechanisms are integrated with Omnigent helpers/tools, not a demonstrated generic wrapper for our manual subscription TUI/agy seats.
Must replay actual provider traffic, verify trust/certificate handling and Google endpoint isolation.
Linux helper seccomp blocks creation of new namespaces; reuse does not automatically cure nested Codex sandbox failures.
Default backend selection can choose none when Linux bwrap is missing; qualify an explicit required profile.

upstream_reuse.name: Windows
limits: This backend explicitly does not enforce filesystem or network isolation. A remote Linux sandbox remains a candidate; do not report native Windows profile parity.

upstream_reuse.name: E2B adapter
provides: upload, streaming command handles and termination
limits: Control credentials are normally read from environment, unlike the harness plan's owner-only key-file contract.
Creates with omnigent-name metadata, not the harness owner/lease reservation/fence protocol.
Command timeout is disabled for install/clone operations; adapter must enforce harness deadline/output bounds.
No generic per-placement egress attestation, snapshot verification or kill-by-lease fencing.

agent_harness: exact staged snapshot and source identity
placement state machine, one execution owner and no retry after uncertain launch
deadline/output limits and grounded seat evidence
omnigent: sandbox host provisioning and optional managed execution
file transfer and process transport where supported
provider lifecycle and optional managed warm pools
configured tool sandbox and egress/credential proxy

recommended_next_work: Map the current ExecutingBackend requirements to one upstream SandboxLifecycle/ExecTransport provider, naming gaps rather than treating capability booleans as proof.

Preserve the owner-approved SSH-first order; choose whether upstream primitive reuse belongs in the SSH guest/control implementation or in the already-planned cloud follow-on. Do not silently substitute a new control plane.

Build one qualification path with no live provider account: transfer exact stage, independently verify digest, execute a harmless owned workload, return bounded receipt, renew, cancel, confirm release and reject a late execution after kill.
Qualify one real required review leg on that same path with subscription identity, tools, known output and correctly recorded seat capabilities.
Evaluate upstream egress/credential proxy against Gemini's actual inference protocol and hostile alternate-host/direct-egress cases before promising tools.
Reconcile older Omnigent backing and TypeScript transport version contracts before treating either as a production sandbox integration.
